title: Discovering sentence types
summary: Recognise and use Spanish statements, questions, exclamations and commands or requests in everyday situations.
keyIdeas: Statements affirm or deny something. The written statements in these exercises end with a full stop.
Direct Spanish questions use ¿? and exclamations use ¡! to express emotion or surprise.
Imperative sentences can give commands, make requests or give instructions.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas de producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: Hugo says «Hoy tenemos Educación Física en el patio». What type of Spanish sentence is this?
activities.explanation: Hugo gives information in a positive statement. The Spanish type is «enunciativa afirmativa».
activities.hint: Is he giving information or asking a question?

activities.prompt: In Spanish, direct written questions use both an opening mark (¿) and a closing mark (?).
activities.explanation: Direct questions need both marks. In «No sé cuándo viene», the question is indirect and does not use them.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish sentence to Aisha's purpose.
activities.explanation: Exclamation marks express emotion, question marks frame questions, and imperative sentences ask for or command something.

pairs.right: Make a request or give a command

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish sentences into positive or negative statements.
activities.explanation: Positive statements affirm something. Negative statements use words such as «no» or «nunca» to deny it.

items.text: El autobús escolar ya ha llegado.
Mañana visitaremos el museo de ciencias.

activities.prompt: Choose the Spanish word to turn this positive statement into a negative statement.
activities.explanation: «no» denies the action and makes the sentence a negative statement.
activities.sentence: Mateo ___ quiere llegar tarde al entrenamiento de baloncesto.

activities.prompt: Find the Spanish sentence with a punctuation mistake.
activities.explanation: The opening question mark is missing. Write «¿Cuándo termina la película de animación?».
activities.hint: Direct Spanish questions need opening and closing marks.
options: ¿Quieres venir a merendar a mi casa?
¡Menuda sorpresa nos ha dado el abuelo!
Cuándo termina la película de animación?

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish conversation between Leo and Martina in the library.
activities.explanation: Each character's purpose helps us recognise the type of sentence used.
activities.title: Tarde en la biblioteca
activities.text: Leo y Martina entraron en la biblioteca del barrio después de merendar. La sala estaba muy tranquila. Martina vio un libro sobre dinosaurios en una estantería alta. Con voz suave le preguntó a su amigo: «¿Me ayudas a alcanzar ese libro verde?». Leo sonrió, se estiró y lo cogió con cuidado. Al abrirlo, Martina exclamó entusiasmada: «¡Tiene unas ilustraciones increíbles!». El bibliotecario se acercó despacio y les susurró amablemente: «Por favor, guardad silencio para no molestar a los demás lectores». Los dos asintieron y se sentaron juntos a leer.

questions.prompt: What is Martina's purpose when she says «¿Me ayudas a alcanzar ese libro verde?»?
questions.explanation: It is a question that Martina uses to ask Leo for help.
options: Warn that the book is broken.
Give an angry command to the librarian.
Ask Leo a question to request his help.

questions.prompt: What type of sentence does the librarian use in «Por favor, guardad silencio»?
questions.explanation: The librarian makes a polite request using an imperative sentence.

activities.prompt: The teacher needs to begin the lesson. Which Spanish imperative sentence is suitable and respectful?
activities.explanation: It gives a clear instruction politely, using «por favor».
activities.hint: Find a sentence giving an instruction or request to the class.
options: Abrid el cuaderno por la página diez, por favor.
¿Quién ha abierto el cuaderno por la página diez?
¡Qué bonito es este cuaderno de rayas!

activities.prompt: Put these Spanish words in order to make a correct direct question.
activities.explanation: The question begins with ¿ and a capital letter, and ends with ?: «¿Has visto a mi perro Tobi?».

activities.prompt: Adrián watches heavy rain through the window and feels surprised. Which Spanish exclamation expresses this?
activities.explanation: «¡Cómo llueve esta tarde!» uses exclamation marks and expresses Adrián's surprise strongly.
activities.hint: Find the choice showing emotion with exclamation marks.
options: Esta tarde apenas caen cuatro gotas.
